h1: Andorra la Vella travel, stays & events guide
heroText: Andorra la Vella is a compact Pyrenean capital built around shopping streets, mountain roads and thermal water. Base yourself near Avinguda Meritxell for restaurants, walk to Casa de la Vall for old Andorran politics, then book Caldea for an easy spa evening. Most arrivals use Barcelona-El Prat or Toulouse-Blagnac, with road transfers over the mountains.

areas.name: Avinguda Meritxell
areas.text: Avinguda Meritxell is the main shopping spine, close to hotels, restaurants and bus stops for a first Andorra stay.

areas.name: Barri Antic
areas.text: Barri Antic is the small old quarter around Casa de la Vall, better for atmosphere than large hotel choice.

areas.name: Escaldes-Engordany
areas.text: Escaldes-Engordany sits beside the capital with Caldea, spa hotels and quick walks back into the centre.

areas.name: La Massana
areas.text: La Massana is outside the capital but useful for ski access, mountain biking and quieter apartment stays.

airports.name: Andorra-La Seu d'Urgell Airport (LEU)
airports.search: Andorra-La Seu d'Urgell Airport, La Seu d'Urgell, Spain
airports.text: Andorra-La Seu is the closest airport, mainly useful for limited regional services and private aviation near the Spanish border.

airports.name: Barcelona-El Prat Airport (BCN)
airports.text: Barcelona-El Prat is the main international gateway for Andorra, with regular bus and private transfers through the Pyrenees.

airportTransfer.value: 3-4 hours by bus or private transfer from Barcelona-El Prat
airportTransfer.note: Andorra has no major commercial airport

stayOverview: Stay around Avinguda Meritxell for shops and restaurants, Barri Antic for a small historic feel, Escaldes-Engordany for Caldea and spa hotels, or La Massana when skiing and mountain access matter more than city-centre walks.
hotelIntro: Andorra hotel choice is mostly about trip purpose: central Andorra la Vella suits shopping weekends, Escaldes-Engordany suits spa stays, and La Massana or other valley towns suit ski lifts and summer trails.
rentalCars: A car helps for ski villages and viewpoints, but central Andorra la Vella is walkable once you arrive.

travelTips.title: Best base
travelTips.text: Choose Avinguda Meritxell for the easiest first stay, especially if you arrive by bus from Barcelona or Toulouse.

travelTips.title: Transfer planning
travelTips.text: Mountain roads make airport transfers long, so avoid tight same-day flight connections from Barcelona or Toulouse.

travelTips.title: Spa timing
travelTips.text: Book Caldea ahead on weekends and winter holidays, when spa sessions and nearby hotels fill quickly.

travelTips.title: Season
travelTips.text: Winter is ski-focused, while summer and early autumn are better for hiking, cycling and clear mountain views.

history.label: Origins
history.text: The site of Andorra la Vella has been settled since prior to the Christian era—notably by the Andosin tribe from the late Neolithic.
The settlement of Andorra la Vella has been the principal city of Andorra since 1278 when the French and the Episcopal co-princes agreed to joint suzerainty.
Its most notable building is the Casa de la Vall—constructed in the early sixteenth century—which has been the state's parliamentary house since 1702.

history.label: 1930s
history.text: After political turmoil in the 1930s and an attempted coup by Boris Skossyreff, an informal democracy developed.
It also hosted both the 1991 and 2005 Games of the Small States of Europe.
In 1993, the country's first constitution formalised this parliamentary democracy with executive, legislative, and judicial branches located in Andorra la Vella.
The city also developed its skiing facilities, to the extent that Andorra la Vella was Andorra's applicant city for the XXI Olympic Winter Games, the 2010 Winter Olympics.

history.label: Growth
history.text: Andorra was part of the County of Urgell, one of the Catalan counties of the Marca Hispanica created by Charlemagne in the eighth century as a buffer from the Moorish settlers in the Iberian.

history.label: Regional role
history.text: Andorra la Vella was, during this period, the capital of a largely isolated and feudal lordship within the Principality of Catalonia, which retained its existence due to this principle of co-sovereignty.

history.label: Regional role
history.text: Well into the twentieth century, the area around Andorra la Vella remained largely forgotten.

history.label: Regional role
history.text: During this period, Andorra also developed as a tax haven, resulting in the construction of modern banking offices in Andorra La Vella.

history.label: Regional role
history.text: However, Andorra la Vella was not selected by the IOC as a candidate city, following the evaluation report of an IOC commission.
